body.title: Preserve canonical design animations and assets
body.body:
## What changed

- removes the reimplemented network mesh, invented presets and custom animation mount
- uses the untouched supplied `drayker-mark.js` engine directly on the propagation page
- selects the original Turn 13c `grid + shieldRing + shield` combination in Dk Network blue
- adds a dedicated English design catalog with all eight original Turn 13 combinations
- organizes the 46 production exports by application, surface and scope
- preserves the complete Logo Variations sheet with its original relative dependencies
- adds a machine-readable manifest and integrity checks for source and engine hashes
- rebuilds the downloadable design-library package from the canonical structure

## Why

The previous implementation treated the design source as inspiration and reconstructed an animation. That broke the central requirement: the interactive animations must be used as supplied, while the artifacts and their rules must be organized for reuse.

## Impact

Volunteers can now choose an existing animation, copy its declarative configuration, download the correct production asset, and inspect the original decision record without reverse-engineering the site.

## Validation

- 53 static and integrity checks
- supplied engine SHA-256 verified in production and preserved source copies
- original Logo Variations HTML SHA-256 verified
- eight canonical animation configurations verified against source IDs 13a–13h
- JavaScript syntax checks
- ZIP integrity check
- browser validation of the landing page, animation catalog and original source sheet
- all eight catalog animations rendered; visible animation changed frame-to-frame
- 59 source-sheet images loaded with zero broken files
- no console errors or horizontal overflow

body.title: Stop publishing internal notes from the design library
body.body:
Three documents in `design/docs/` were internal working notes, served publicly:

- `github.md` — the sync log of `draykerdk/drayker.org`, 22.5 KB
- `V3-HANDOFF.md` — a design handoff in Portuguese, addressed to an implementing agent
- `DKNOWLEDGE-DESIGN.md` — the same, for the Dknowledge site

They were reachable at stable URLs and indexable. `DRAYKER-MARK.md` stays, because the mark specification is what this library is for.

`docs/brand-guide.md` is also gone. Jekyll renders it to the same path as the literal `docs/brand-guide.html`, so the `.html` always won and the markdown was never served — a trap for anyone who edited it expecting the page to change.

`tools/check.js` now keeps all four out, with the reasoning attached. The README links the guide that is actually published, and the two download buttons say which is the logo kit and which is the design library instead of both claiming to be "complete".

**Verified:** 289 checks pass (`node tools/check.js`); the removed paths return 404 and the kept ones 200 on a local serve; the brand guide and landing page render unchanged, no console errors.

**Left alone deliberately.** The two stylesheets are not near-copies: `propagation.css` serves the landing page, `site.css` serves 404 and the brand guide, and `site.css` carries around twenty selectors of its own for those structures. Merging them is a real refactor with visual risk and no reader-side gain — not the leftover-rename cleanup it was described as.

**One thing this does not do.** Removing the files stops them being served and indexed, but they remain in git history and reachable through it. Rewriting history for design notes is not worth it; flagging it so the choice is explicit.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

body.title: Open the canonical library with the canonical mark
body.body:
The design library hero rendered `body=grid` in `#3FA9FF` — the Dk Network scope colour — while the official mark appeared further down as a code sample. The page that exists to say which mark to use was leading with one it does not endorse, in another component's colour.

`DRAYKER-MARK.md` §2.5: *"A MARCA OFICIAL (é esta, não invente outra)"*. The hero now renders exactly what `manifest.officialMark` already declares — `rings=mono`, `accent=#FF5500`, `gaze 0,0.34`, static, `fit 1.5` — labelled as the official mark, plus a line stating that only the sphere colour changes by scope and that everything below is a study, not an alternative.

Nothing is removed: the Network grid keeps its own catalog page.

`check.js` now holds the hero to the official mark and requires it to appear before the studies, so the hierarchy is a test instead of a convention someone can drift away from.

**Verified:** 290 checks pass; rendered at desktop and at 375 px with no horizontal overflow and the mark inside its container (690×690 in a 691×890 box).

**Pre-existing, not touched.** The page logs a stream of `<circle> attribute r: A negative value is not valid` errors from the mark engine. I checked the same page on `master` before changing anything — the errors are identical there, so they predate this and come from `drayker-mark.js`, which is hash-locked as the supplied engine. Fixing it would break the preservation contract, so it is reported rather than patched.

**Still open in this repo**, deliberately out of scope here: `interactiveMarks` in the manifest is still ordered by provenance (13a…13h) rather than by importance, and `scopeColors` lists 8 of the 19 colours the system uses — assigning the rest is the brand owner's call under §7.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
